# Facewise concave velocities and the visible-star dual restriction

This note answers a specific question about the actual visible-star construction. Its regular first-order optimality condition follows already from the archived physical boundary martingale. Thus these deformations do not provide an additional quantitative inequality beyond that certificate. This is an exact obstruction to a proposed proof mechanism, not an obstruction to OC.

## 1. A facewise Jensen theorem

Let `C` be a polytope with a finite integer base and positive full-dimensional continuous fibers. Let `eta` be the sum of fiber surface measures, marked with each regular point's unique outward continuous unit normal. In dimension one this is the measure on the two endpoints with their respective normals. Let `nu=f eta` be nonnegative and suppose there is a physical martingale coupling from `nu` to `eta`: each source row at `(z,x)` has physical mean `(z,x)`.

Every row stays in every ambient support face containing its source point. Indeed, an ambient facet inequality is nonnegative in gap form throughout `C`, and its expected gap is its gap at the source. If this is zero, the row is concentrated on that face. The coupling also preserves the continuous unit normal at almost every regular boundary point, as proved in `candidate 7278f286325c46c7`, Section 5. Both conclusions concern actual fiber boundaries, not independent abstract surfaces.

Suppose a bounded Borel function `g` on the marked boundary has the following property: for each nonvertical ambient facet `F`, there is a continuous concave function `g_F` on `F` agreeing with `g` at `eta`-almost every point of that facet whose continuous normal is its normalized continuous facet normal. Then

    integral g dnu >= integral g deta.               (1)

Proof. At a regular fiber-boundary source, choose the first nonvertical ambient facet containing it whose normalized continuous normal equals its fiber normal. Such a facet exists for a polytope. The finite choice is Borel. The conditional target row stays in that face and keeps the same continuous normal; since its second marginal is `eta`, the agreement with `g_F` holds almost surely. Jensen's inequality for `g_F` and the physical row barycenter gives

    g(source)>=E[g(target)|source].

Integration proves (1). This argument handles positive mixed measure on an intersection of several ambient facets: it chooses a real containing face, and the entire row stays in that face. No ambient-null set is discarded.

The hypothesis does not say that `g` extends to a concave function on all of `C`. That stronger condition is unnecessary. The face-preserving support of the transport is the decisive input.

## 2. Every actual visible-star velocity has the required concavity

Use the definitions and exact representative rule of Section 6 of `candidate 92bb4f0b51f51e22`. For a continuous displacement of `w0` and a visible facet `F`, the actual outward normal velocity is

    g_F(w)=(u_F.v) T_(F,w0)(w),                      (2)

where `u_F.v>0` and `T_(F,w0)` is the concave homothetic facet roof. For a nonvisible facet put `g_F=0`.

These facewise functions agree with the actual fiber normal velocity `g` almost everywhere. Distinct nonparallel continuous normals meet in fiber-codimension at least two and have zero fiber surface measure. At a positive-surface-measure seam of equal continuous normals, two visible roofs agree by the exact seam lemma. At an intersection of a visible and a nonvisible facet with the same continuous normal, the visible roof is zero: if the nonvisible facet contains `w0`, visibility would agree; otherwise its affine gap is strictly positive at `w0`, and a positive homothetic coefficient of `w0` cannot land in that facet. Thus the zero value is also consistent.

Consequently the added-volume measure `xi` of the star is exactly `g eta`, including its representative convention at discrete seams. Applying (1) proves

    integral g(f-1) deta >=0                          (3)

for every visible-star velocity and every such boundary martingale certificate. The same conclusion holds for any other actual velocity satisfying the stated facewise concavity and agreement properties.

## 3. Exact identification with the critical-circuit dual

Here assume the regular critical-cap and threshold hypotheses of Section 3 of the shared-facet note. For group `i`, let its positive circuit coefficients be `rho_ij`, its cap section measures be `S_ij>0`, and define

    theta_ij=(rho_ij/S_ij)/(sum_l rho_il/S_il),
    W_i=sum_j theta_ij 1_(H_ij).

Suppose the normalized extremal stress has nonnegative group weights `Lambda_i` and the matching density

    f=sum_i Lambda_i W_i,
    sum_i Lambda_i=1/beta.                            (4)

This is the regular form of the archived cap stress. To see the group normalization directly, all signed threshold variations with `sum_j rho_ij s_ij=0` preserve the group's cover. A stress annihilating those signed variations satisfies `lambda_ij S_ij=constant_i rho_ij`. Therefore `lambda_ij=Lambda_i theta_ij`. Summing the cap weights gives (4).

For the actual visible-star deformation, write `A=integral g deta`. Its regular reoptimized cap response is

    R_i=tau_i'(0+)-beta M'(0+)
       =integral g(W_i-beta) deta.

Equations (3)–(4) now give the exact dual restriction

    sum_i Lambda_i R_i
       =integral g(f-1) deta >=0.                    (5)

Thus one group has nonnegative response whenever at least one stress weight is positive. No common strictly descending star is possible in the presence of this already existing certificate. This conclusion is not an extra inequality one can combine with convex order to obtain a contradiction: it is a consequence of convex order together with actual face support.

Positive cap/body facet coincidences remain outside this regular identification. The facewise Jensen theorem (1) itself still holds for a boundary measure with consistent allocations, but relating its value to a particular nonsmooth cap response requires the actual allocation quantifiers. This note does not choose those allocations freely or interchange their existential and universal roles.

## 4. Where strictness occurs, and what is not forced

For a polyhedral concave roof `g_F=min_r ell_r`, choose an affine piece active at a source point `w`. The row Jensen gap is exactly

    g_F(w)-E g_F(Y)=E[ell_r(Y)-g_F(Y)] >=0.          (6)

It vanishes if and only if the row is supported on the contact set where this active piece equals the roof. The same criterion holds for every active piece at `w`. A row spreading across a genuinely bent part of the roof has positive gap.

Local minimality only asks for the nonnegative weighted response (5); it does not require that response to vanish. Therefore (6) cannot force transport to become deterministic or to stay in every tent's affine cell. Such a rigidity claim would need a separately proved opposite variation or a higher-order equality condition. The new star construction supplies neither automatically.

The remaining useful geometric information is the actual anchored support equality and common-face cap geometry of each martingale row. The all-status anchored residual inequalities add genuine bulk constraints to those rows. This note shows why merely adding first-order face-concave outward deformations cannot convert those necessary conditions into the missing sharp numerical bound.
